objective: Test whether advancing to later, previously unsampled training patient groups improves the selected OCT candidate.

hypothesis.statement: Previous continuations replayed the opening patient groups. Rotating the per-class schedule by 50 should expose new training groups while preserving label balance and the frozen test boundary.
hypothesis.result: Not supported. New groups reduced training loss at some steps but did not improve generated-label macro-F1; the first declined validation check triggered early stopping.

reason: The first step lowered loss to 0.0349831771 but task macro-F1 and OCT macro-F1 remained exactly at the entry values.
Steps 5 and 10 also held exactly while loss rose, so the best checkpoint remained an unchanged classification result.
Step 15 declined to macro-F1 0.8677248677 and OCT 0.7746031746; the new-groups run then triggered early stopping.
The Stage-5 best_adapter is not a meaningful promotion and the final adapter is not a deployment artifact.
limitations: The 55-row validation screen covers 33 groups and cannot reliably identify small class-level gains.
Successful group rotation proves that new training patients were scheduled; it does not prove improved generalization.
Frozen test images were not read during training or schedule selection.
The experiment is a research result, not patient-isolated external validation or clinical evidence.
next_step: Do not start another same-panel continuation. Freeze the step-20 research candidate and obtain patient-isolated validation or clinician-reviewed labels before another training round.
